chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali al-Hannat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What is the reward for the one who trims his moustache and clips his nails every Friday?' He said, 'He remains purified until the next Friday.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for trimming nails and moustache every Friday in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical act of grooming—specifically trimming the moustache and clipping nails—to a sustained state of ritual purity (mutahhar) that endures until the next Friday. This highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating personal hygiene (fitrah) with spiritual cleanliness, viewing regular grooming not merely as a habit but as a means of maintaining a continuous state of preparedness for worship and divine proximity.
